prompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: text-free landscape cover art for Whitechapel, a grounded cooperative detective game set in London, 16 November 1888.
Primary request: An immersive atmospheric view from the damp cobbled lane into the welcoming yet worn common room of the fictional Lantern inn in Whitechapel at dusk. Modest soot-dark London brick frontage, timber door open a little, sash windows, amber gaslight inside, an iron lantern by the entrance. Through the window only the suggestion of a woman doing needlework at a small table. Narrow passage leads toward a rear service yard; a simple wooden coal handcart is barely visible there. No actual surveyed street or historical landmark.
Style/medium: richly textured painterly realism for a mature historical investigation game, muted ink black, slate blue, warm subdued amber, tactile brick and weathered wood; quiet cinematic composition, realistic Victorian working-class London, not gothic fantasy.
Composition/framing: wide landscape 16:9, eye-level from the lane, the Lantern at center-right and gentle darkness at left for game title added separately. Full-bleed finished cover image.
Lighting/mood: November blue hour, damp reflective cobbles, low pools of gaslight, ordinary life and melancholy, no supernatural glow.
Constraints: No writing, lettering, signs with text, UI, logos, watermark, detectives, police, bodies, gore, blood, menace, weapons, electric streetlights, motorcars, modern objects, medieval timber facade, orange parchment, exaggerated fog. This is a fictional inn, not a historical facsimile.

Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: fictional mounted wedding photograph for an 1888 detective game, photographed originally in 1884. Generate a complete authentic-looking 1884 British studio wedding portrait on an ivory card, full physical card seen straight from above on a narrow charcoal background. Three people full length, mother on LEFT, bride at CENTER, groom on RIGHT separated enough that a tear just right of the bride would remove ONLY the groom. Bride Nora Finch, age 26, oval pale face, dark auburn brown hair simply pinned, ordinary modest ivory dress with high collar, tiny bouquet, no extravagant veil. Her mother age 58, grey hair center-parted in bun, plain dark dress. Groom Arthur Vale about age30, short dark hair, narrow dark moustache, angular face, broadish build average height, respectable dark charcoal coat and waistcoat. All white English working-class people with unsmiling formal expressions, standing facing camera. Simple painted studio drapery backdrop and wooden chair, restrained faded warm grey albumen tones, subtle old photograph grain, material realism, exact faces clear enough for recognition. No writing, labels, date, ornamented frame, modern photograph colors, watermark, tears or damage. Entire intact card border visible.

Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: an invented 1888 sensational illustrated newspaper wood engraving; monochrome ink drawing, no lettering. A non-graphic distant fully clothed woman lies still on her side in a narrow London brick yard, ordinary dark Victorian working dress covers her completely, with a pale scarf laid across and covering her entire face. The scarf is obvious and crosses face horizontally, face concealed. Constable at far entrance with lantern observing from a respectful distance. No wounds, no blood, no exposed anatomy, no horror detail, no murderer. Black wood-engraved hatching, period newspaper illustrative style, rectangular composition, opaque ivory background. The image represents a fictional newspaper artist's imagined scene, not a true historical crime scene. Scarf positioning is the crucial clue. No text, no captions, no border, no watermark.

A large travel-worn wooden travelling trunk with iron corners, black leather straps and broad hinged lid closed, approximately 110cm long, beside the rear service door of a modest London inn. Painterly photorealism with tactile materials, muted slate, umber, subdued amber. Ordinary solid Victorian luggage with no printed labels or text, no padlock and no decorative fantasy fittings. No body, no people, no blood, no weapons, no modern objects, no watermark. This is the initial closed view of a trunk, do not show contents.

Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: detailed inspection art for Whitechapel 1888. A modest small room in the rear extension of a fictional London inn.
